solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mechanical ear's covered by fleece

indicators.note: in a down clue the piece for the ear sits below, covered by, the piece for fleece

parts.note: to fleece someone is to rob or swindle them
otic is the adjective meaning of or relating to the ear

explanation.surface: A mechanic's ear is tucked under a woolly fleece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleece' looks like a sheep's coat but is the verb to rob. 'Covered by' places OTIC under ROB in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mechanical moves in an automatic, machine-like way, as a robot would.

clue.text: Beauty clasping trimmed gemstone trinket

indicators.note: clasping means the word for beauty holds the other piece within it

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman, a beauty

indicators.note: trimmed means the word for the gemstone loses its final letter

parts.note: agate is a banded semi-precious gemstone

explanation.surface: A beautiful woman wears a cut gem as a little ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beauty' looks like a quality of the gem, but it names a beautiful woman; 'trimmed' and 'clasping' then do the work.
explanation.definitionFit: A bagatelle is a thing of little value, a mere trifle or bauble.

clue.text: Incantation when source of danger loses power

indicators.note: loses means the letter for power is taken away from the longer word

parts.note: a mantrap is a trap for catching trespassers, a source of danger
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A spell becomes harmless once the danger behind it loses its power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loses' removes P from MANTRAP; 'when' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a word or phrase chanted repeatedly, as in meditation or prayer.

clue.text: Gifted toughie consuming beer and books

indicators.note: consuming means the word for the tough swallows the other letters

parts.note: a Ted, short for Teddy boy, was a tough young man of 1950s Britain
ale is a kind of beer
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A clever thug downs beer while reading.
explanation.walkthrough: A Teddy boy was a 1950s British youth known for Edwardian dress and a tough reputation; 'consuming' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Being gifted means having natural ability, a synonym for being talented.

clue.text: French fries costing less? It's a critical situation

definitions.meaning: chips whose price has gone down, read literally
an idiom said when a decisive, testing moment has arrived

explanation.surface: Cheaper fries might seem like a crisis to some.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part reads the idiom literally, with chips as fried potatoes and down meaning lower in price.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom, from gambling chips being placed, means the moment of crisis when action is needed.

clue.text: Rarely it can be associated with writing

indicators.note: can be suggests the letters may be made into something else by rearranging them

explanation.surface: A rarely seen thing might be tied to authorship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can be' signals the anagram of RARELY IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary describes things concerning books, authors and written works.

clue.text: In city regularly banning butter

indicators.note: In tells us the regular letters go inside the city's abbreviation

parts.note: NY is New York, the city

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of banning is taken

explanation.surface: A city regularly bans butter from its shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes A, N, N from bAnNiNg; 'In' places them within NY.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanny goat butts, so it is jokingly a butter, one who butts.

clue.text: Choose nursing team members for constant factor

indicators.note: nursing means the word for choose takes the team members into itself
for means the team members stand in place of the letter for constant

parts.note: to elect is to choose by vote
c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
men are members of a team

explanation.surface: Picking hospital staff as a steady part of the plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nursing' and 'for' together put MEN into ELECT where its C was. 'Constant factor' reads as one phrase, but 'constant' gives C and only 'factor' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An element is a component or contributing part, just as a factor is.

clue.text: Composition some charlatan ostensibly rejected

indicators.note: rejected means the letters taken are turned back to front
some means a few letters are taken from within the words charlatan ostensibly

explanation.surface: A fraud's work was, on the face of it, turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks ATANOS from charlATAN OStensibly; 'rejected' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonata is a musical work, a composition for one or a few instruments.

clue.text: Lengthy message, lacking opening, reached conclusion

indicators.note: lacking opening means the word for message loses its first letter

parts.note: a text is a message sent by phone
to have ended is to have reached a conclusion

explanation.surface: A long message, missing its start, finally came to an end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking opening' cuts TEXT to EXT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extended has been lengthened or drawn out, so is long.

clue.text: Chivalrous tale with idiosyncratic feature relating to love

parts.note: a roman is a medieval verse romance of chivalry, from the French
a tic is a habitual quirk or idiosyncrasy

explanation.surface: A knightly story with a quirky touch turns out to be about love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chivalrous' tempts as the definition, but the knightly story gives ROMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Romantic describes things to do with love or amorous feeling.

clue.text: What boy does with toy in nursery verses?

definitions.meaning: the word boy sounds alike at the end with the word toy
nursery verses are short poems for children with chiming lines

explanation.surface: A child playing with a toy in the nursery as songs are sung.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boy' and 'toy' are words here, not a child and a plaything.
explanation.definitionFit: Nursery rhymes are traditional children's poems, and verses that chime at the ends are also so named.

clue.text: Smart figures organised rite in clipped language

indicators.note: in means the rearranged rite goes inside the clipped language
clipped means the language's name has its last letter cut off

parts.note: Latin is a classical language

indicators.note: organised means the letters of rite are arranged differently

explanation.surface: Well-dressed people stage a ceremony in abbreviated Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' suggests well dressed but means clever here; the rearranged rite sits after the first letter of the clipped language.
explanation.definitionFit: The literati are educated, intellectual people, smart in the clever sense.

clue.text: Undressed football club bigwigs in goals?

indicators.note: undressed means the club's name is stripped of its outer letters

parts.note: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club
suits is slang for executives, the bigwigs of an organisation

explanation.surface: A football club's bosses caught without their clothes at the goalmouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is Tottenham Hotspur, an English football club. 'Undressed' strips SPURS to PUR. 'Goals' plays on football but means aims.
explanation.definitionFit: Pursuits are things one strives after, aims or objectives, here clued as goals.

clue.text: Lacking in schooling turned out problematic

indicators.note: problematic suggests the letters of turned out have been thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Having missed school turned out to cause trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Problematic' signals the anagram of TURNED OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone untutored has received no formal teaching or education.

clue.text: Creation with numerous gaps in book by old author?

indicators.note: by means the book's word is placed beside the old author's letters

parts.note: a pen stands for a writer, an author
a book is a work, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: A book by a writer of long ago is full of holes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link word joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Openwork is ornamental fabric or metal with holes or spaces in its pattern, like lace.

clue.text: Small empty township surrounded by marine plant

indicators.note: surrounded by means the inner letters are enclosed by the word for marine

parts.note: marine means of the sea
wee is Scottish for small

indicators.note: empty means only the outside letters of township are kept

explanation.surface: A little deserted town is ringed by seaweed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marine plant' reads as seaweed, but 'marine' is wordplay and 'plant' alone defines; 'empty' keeps only the ends of township.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet pea is a climbing garden plant grown for its scented flowers.

clue.text: Evaluates, it's said, most of plan for border

indicators.note: it's said marks a word that is spoken and spelt another way

parts.note: to weigh up is to evaluate

indicators.note: most of means the word for plan drops its last letter

parts.note: an idea is a plan

explanation.surface: Someone weighs up most of a scheme for the edge of the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's said' turns WEIGHS into WAYS; 'most of' trims IDEA to IDE.
explanation.definitionFit: The wayside is the edge or verge of a road, a border.

clue.text: Twisted journalist supporting singular gang

indicators.note: in a down clue supporting puts the journalist's letters below the rest

parts.note: S is the grammar abbreviation for singular
a crew is a gang
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A crooked newspaperman backs one odd gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supporting' places ED under S and CREW in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Screwed means turned round and round, twisted, as a screw is.

clue.text: Drink from odd sock

parts.note: rum is an old British word for odd or strange
to sock is to punch

explanation.surface: A beverage pulled out of a mismatched sock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd sock' suggests an unpaired garment; here odd and sock are separate synonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum punch is a mixed alcoholic drink of rum, juice and spice.

clue.text: Very great age of octogenarian, male, not English

indicators.note: not means the letter for English is removed

parts.note: an octogenarian is in their eighties, so eighty is such an age

explanation.surface: An old man of eighty, not an Englishman, reaches a grand age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not English' takes E from EIGHTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Mighty means powerful or huge in scale, a synonym for very great.

clue.text: Battling conformity, troubled firm drops top executive

indicators.note: battling suggests the letters of conformity are in conflict and thrown about
troubled tells us the letters of firm are mixed in as well
drops means the letters of firm leave the jumbled pool

explanation.surface: A struggling company fighting conformity sacks its boss.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of FIRM out of CONFORMITY and rearrange what is left, CONOTY.
explanation.definitionFit: A tycoon is a wealthy, powerful business magnate, a head of industry.

clue.text: Swine decapitated water creature

indicators.note: decapitated means the word for swine loses its first letter

parts.note: a rotter is a contemptible person, a swine

explanation.surface: A headless pig floating in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swine' looks like a pig but means a rotten person.
explanation.definitionFit: The otter is an aquatic mammal living in rivers and coasts.

clue.text: Philanthropist, setter, say, rounds on upset friend now and then

parts.note: a setter is a breed of dog, so an example of one
O is a round shape, so two rounds are OO

indicators.note: upset in an across clue means the letters chosen are turned back
now and then means taking every other letter of friend

explanation.surface: A charitable crossword compiler circles back to a troubled friend from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' seems to be the crossword's compiler, but it is a dog. 'Now and then' takes RED from fRiEnD; 'upset' reverses it to DER.
explanation.definitionFit: A do-gooder is a well-meaning person devoted to helping others, a philanthropist.

clue.text: Six tours organised with opera's principal star performer

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: organised means the letters of tours are put in a new order
principal means the first letter of opera's is taken

explanation.surface: Six concert tours are arranged around an opera's leading singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organised' turns TOURS into RTUOS; 'principal' takes O from opera's.
explanation.definitionFit: A virtuoso is a performer of outstanding skill, a star in their field.

clue.text: Restrain revolutionary in ranks

parts.note: to tie someone up is to restrain them
a red is a communist, a revolutionary

explanation.surface: Holding back a rebel within the army's lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In ranks' defines a word meaning arranged in rows, one above another.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiered means set out in rows or layers rising one behind another, like seats.

clue.text: Something to wear having reported naked flesh?

indicators.note: reported tells us the phrase for naked flesh is spoken, giving a word spelt another way

parts.note: naked flesh is bare skin

explanation.surface: Someone wearing nothing but their own bare skin.
explanation.walkthrough: A bearskin is the tall fur cap of British guards regiments, as seen at Buckingham Palace.
explanation.definitionFit: A bearskin is a tall black fur hat, a piece of headgear worn by guardsmen.
